messages:
Maya: Quick summary — ran quant bakeoff on new-llamaX across FP8 / INT8-GPTQ / AWQ. Observing a surprising perf vs accuracy tradeoff when prefix KV cache is enabled together with continuous_batching. p99 spikes for INT8-GPTQ only when both are on. Details below.

Sam: can you paste the configs and the perf table?

Maya: sure — config snippets we used: 
```
model: new-llamaX
seq_len: 1024
batcher: continuous_batching: true
          max_batch_size: 8
cache: prefix_kv_cache: enabled
quant: variants: [fp8, int8-gptq, awq]
profiling: trace_level: brief
```

Maya: Raw perf/quality snapshot (median of 3 runs):
`model | quant | cache | cont_batch | p50_ms | p99_ms | EM_delta`
`llamaX | fp8       | on  | true  | 35  | 120 | +0.0%`
`llamaX | int8-gptq | on  | true  | 30  | 260 | -1.2%`
`llamaX | awq       | on  | true  | 33  | 125 | -0.2%`
`llamaX | int8-gptq | off | true  | 31  | 115 | -0.9%`
`llamaX | int8-gptq | on  | false | 32  | 118 | -0.3%`

Jon: interesting — so both prefix cache and continuous batching together amplify p99 for INT8-GPTQ. AWQ and FP8 unaffected. That EM -1.2% is concerning too.

Priya: hypothesis: the INT8-GPTQ kernel has sensitivity to KV cache alignment or intermittent token padding that continuous batching exposes (mixed sequences in batch). Maybe the cache replay/concatenation path hits a quantization threshold causing small distribution shift.

Maya: agree. I dug into traces — when cont_batch=true we reuse cached KV slices from earlier requests that were generated under different per-request effective scales. See log snippet: 
```
[2025-05-14T14:22:01Z] request id=run-433 segment=kv_reuse quant_mode=int8-gptq scale_est=0.98
[2025-05-14T14:22:01Z] request id=run-434 segment=kv_reuse quant_mode=int8-gptq scale_est=1.12
[2025-05-14T14:22:01Z] merge_kv -> applying rescale fudge=0.93
[2025-05-14T14:22:02Z] forward -> p99 jump observed
```

Arjun: can you reproduce by forcing fixed batch sizes and deterministic padding? If the issue is mixing sequences with different dynamic ranges, fixed batching should reduce it.

Maya: tested that: fixed_batch=1 (no mixing) + prefix_cache=on -> p99 back to ~120 and EM drop reduces to -0.4%. So mixing appears to be the trigger.

Sam: next experiments?

Maya: proposed run list: 
1) INT8-GPTQ: cont_batch=true, prefix_cache=on, fixed_batch=false (baseline reproduced)
2) INT8-GPTQ: cont_batch=true, prefix_cache=off
3) INT8-GPTQ: cont_batch=false, prefix_cache=on
4) AWQ: cont_batch=true, prefix_cache=on (control)
5) FP8: same combos (sanity)
Also add per-request scale logging and a rescale-path unit test.

Priya: add a quick micro-benchmark to measure KV value histograms before/after cache merge for int8 vs awq. That'll show distribution shifts.

Maya: yep created runs in perf-lab: run-433 (baseline), run-434 (no-cache), run-435 (no-cont), run-436 (awq-control).

deploy-bot: I started run-433 on infra-perf (g4dn-equivalent). ETA ~ 40m.

infra-bot: note: we've seen similar p99 regressions historically when batching mixes sequences with differing seq_len distributions. Suggest also trying seq_len bucketing and KV normalization layer toggle.

Jon: if this is a kernel-sensitivity issue, long-term fixes: 1) normalize scaling across KV cache (store per-token scale metadata) 2) adjust quantization calibration to be robust to merged caches 3) fall back to fp16 for KV when mismatch detected.

Maya: logging plan: add per-kv-segment scale metadata, histogram dumps, and a small repro that forces two different scale contexts to be merged. If repro looks immediate we'll open an eng-runtime bug and tag inference/quant teams.

Sam: cool — keep updates here. If run-433 reproduces we should schedule a deeper kernel-level profile.

Maya: will post run results and upload traces when done. Thanks all :rocket:
